hook.text: Block codes process data in chunks. Convolutional codes process a continuous stream through a shift register.

buildup.text: A convolutional encoder feeds input bits through a shift register and XORs tapped positions to produce output.

discovery.text: The code has memory: each output depends on the current input and several previous bits. Past context helps.

twist.text: Viterbi decoding finds the most likely sequence of inputs by tracing paths through a trellis diagram.

climax.text: Convolutional codes powered early mobile phones, deep-space links, and dial-up modems. They're streaming-friendly.

punchline.text: Bits flow through memory. Context corrects errors.

quiz.question: How do convolutional codes differ from block codes?
options: They process data as a continuous stream using memory
